close_reason: Refactor landed in d402218. handle_filenode_get and handle_filenode_query no longer extract+reconstitute; they pass args through to the generic handle_get/handle_query and read accountId back from the response shape for post-processing. Other extension-server siblings that use the generic handlers (chat, calendars, addressbook, card, metadata, principal, etc.) already use this pattern — filenode-server now matches the canonical shape.
description:
src/filenode.rs:38-50 (handle_filenode_get) and src/filenode.rs:904-919 (handle_filenode_query) repeat the same dance:

1. extract_account_id(args) → (Id, Map)
2. mutate the Map (reconstitute) by re-inserting accountId
3. call into jmap_server::handlers::handle_get / handle_query with the reconstituted Value::Object

The handler comment at filenode.rs:40-41 admits 'the generic helper re-parses accountId itself, which is fine — the duplicate parse is cheap'. The double parse is not the issue; the issue is that the handler is fighting the extract_account_id signature. Either:

(a) extract_account_id should return both the parsed Id AND the original Value (or a Value-preserving handle) so the handler can both peek at the parsed Id (for backend.get_ancestors / query_subtree) and forward the un-mutated Value to the generic handler. That avoids the reconstitute.

(b) The generic handler in jmap_server::handlers should accept the (Id, Map) tuple directly, removing the reconstitute step.

(c) Refactor: a small helper 'with_account_id<R>(args, |id, args| async { ... }) -> Result<R, JmapError>' that handles the extract-and-keep-args pattern.

Suggested rewrite: option (a). The doc comment 'duplicate parse is cheap' is the kind of comment that should not need to exist — it signals an API mismatch.
title: extract_account_id + reconstitute pattern is repeated boilerplate
